subject: Post-call: Finlytics model-fit checklist and next steps
summary: Recap of discovery call with Finlytics: proposed models, acceptance thresholds for parity to their proprietary baseline, prompt/eval artifacts to run, and mutual action plan for a two-week POC.
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire@finlytics.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@finlytics.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Finlytics model-fit checklist and next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion on the invoice extraction + classification flow and the downstream confidence requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a concrete plan to run model-fit evaluations this week: 

1) Acceptance criteria (you confirmed these on the call):
   - Intent/classification accuracy >= 92% (macro F1 target) versus your in-house baseline on the validation slice we discussed (high-priority vendors).
   - Extraction span recall >= 95% for invoice line items (tolerate precision down to 90% if recall holds).
   - Latency p95 <= 220ms at a 5 TPS sustained traffic profile for production-like batch sizes.

2) Recommended candidate models for the evaluation (we'll run the same prompt set against each):
   - open: Llama-3-70b-q4f32 (Redwood-quant profile) — strong cost/latency tradeoff
   - community: Mistral-xlarge-32k (non-quant) — baseline for open-weight generative quality
   - proprietary baseline (for comparison): Finlytics-v2-prop (your internal production model) — we will use your labeled holdout for parity checks

3) Artifacts we will share today (attached):
   - finlytics_prompt_set_v1.jsonl — canonical prompt templates and 120 labelled examples (validation split)
   - benchmark_results_snapshot.csv — empty template for us to populate after runs
   - mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf — timeline, ownership, and acceptance gates for a 2-week POC

4) Risks / quality regression concerns to watch: 
   - Tokenization divergence between your tokenizer and open models can shift span offsets — we recommend token-level normalization and an offset-mapping check in the eval harness.
   - Quantized model hallucination on low-frequency vendor codes — add targeted prompts and examples in the prompt set (we included 12 hard negatives).
   - Distribution shift between demo invoices and production (multi-page, scanned OCR noise) — propose an OCR augmentation pass during POC.

5) Immediate next steps (action items):
   - Claire: share the 500-record holdout S3 link (s3://finlytics-holdout/invoice-sample-500) and confirm PII redaction status by EOD Monday.
   - Rajiv: confirm whether we can run up to 5K tokens per request for long invoices (yes/no).
   - Dev (cc'd): provision the evaluation stack on Redwood Dedicated with the open candidate models and run the first batch by Wednesday.
   - Neha: provide the evaluation metrics script and acceptance checks; include a canary rollback criterion if F1 drops >3% vs baseline.

Happy to jump on a 30-min tech sync Monday if helpful — otherwise we'll proceed with the POC artifacts attached.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: finlytics_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (jsonl, 12KB), mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

From: Claire Zhang <claire@finlytics.com>

Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@finlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finlytics model-fit checklist and next steps

Thanks Tessa — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. Quick clarifications: 

- We'll share the holdout S3 link by Monday morning (security team will confirm PII redaction; likely redacted but we will provide a token-mapped version if needed).
- We can allow up to 4K tokens per request in the first runs; long-page OCR artifacts we can chunk but will flag any span-splitting issues.
- On the acceptance gates: we want a human-eval sanity check for the top 50 failures (to understand error modes) in addition to the automated metrics.

Let's do the Monday tech sync at 10am PT — I invited Rajiv and our Head of Data (he may hop on for the sanities).

Claire Zhang
Head of Integrations | Finlytics

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Claire Zhang <claire@finlytics.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 07:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finlytics model-fit checklist and next steps

Looping in the infra/bench team notes — first pass plan for running the candidate suite this week: 

- Infra: spin up a small Dedicated cluster (2xA10G) under the deal commit; will run each model with consistent batch settings (batch size 8, seq len 4096 simulated where needed).
- Prompting: we'll run the finlytics_prompt_set_v1.jsonl unchanged first, then an augmented pass with OCR-noise synthetics.
- Metrics: automated metrics will include macro F1 (classification), span recall/precision, normalized edit-distance for spans, and latency p50/p95. We'll also produce a failure export (top 100 mismatches) and a shuffled sample of 50 failures for human review.

Model-specific notes: 
- Llama-3-70b-q4f32 (open) — expected throughput good; watch for small-span offset errors on tokenization. If we hit >2.5% span mismatch we will try a byte-level alignment pass.
- Mistral-xlarge-32k — likely higher quality on ambiguous prompts; expect increased p95 latency.
- Finlytics-v2-prop — we will use this strictly as the reference; runs will be done on your provided artifacts (we do not retain the model).

Rollout safety: if any candidate model drops >3% macro F1 vs the Finlytics baseline on the target slice, we will mark it as not meeting parity and trigger an automatic fallback to the baseline for the canary. That logic is already in our Redwood Console rollout policy — will attach the policy snippet to the evaluation report.

Estimated timeline: first batch completed by EOD Wednesday (2026-11-11 UTC), full POC report and human-eval export by next Tuesday.

- Dev
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: benchmark_results_snapshot.csv (template)
